statutes.title: California Automatic Renewal Law (ARL)
statutes.summary: Requires businesses to clearly disclose automatic renewal terms, obtain affirmative consent, provide an acknowledgment with cancellation terms, and offer a cost-effective, timely, and easy-to-use mechanism for cancellation. As amended by AB 390/SB 313 (2021) and AB 2863 (Stats. 2024, Ch. 515, effective Jan 1, 2025). Post-FTC vacatur, this is the strongest state-level subscription cancellation law. New provisions (effective July 1, 2025) require same-medium cancellation, annual reminders for annual plans, and 7-30 day notice before fee changes.

key_provisions.description: Clear and conspicuous disclosure of the automatic renewal offer terms before the consumer makes the purchase.
Affirmative consent to the automatic renewal before being charged.
An acknowledgment that includes the automatic renewal terms, cancellation policy, and information on how to cancel — in a manner capable of being retained (email).

Provide a cost-effective, timely, and easy-to-use mechanism for cancellation. If accepted online, must be cancellable online. Cannot require the consumer to call or go in person to cancel if signup was online.
For free-trial-to-paid conversions, must notify the consumer before charging and obtain affirmative consent to the paid terms.
Failure to comply: the goods, services, or automatic renewal are deemed an unconditional gift to the consumer, and the consumer is not obligated to pay.
Violation is also a violation of the Unfair Competition Law (Bus. & Prof. Code §17200 et seq.), enabling private right of action.

deadline_rules.action_at_expiry: Send follow-up email if cancellation not confirmed
deadline_rules.description: If the company hasn't confirmed cancellation within 7 days, send the follow-up email.
deadline_rules.prompt_message: Time to send Follow-Up Email 2. Your cancellation request hasn't been confirmed.

penalties.description: If the business fails to comply with the ARL, the goods or services are deemed an unconditional gift — the consumer is not obligated to pay.
penalties.amount_or_formula: Consumer not obligated to pay; charges must be refunded
penalties.conditions: Business failed to properly disclose auto-renewal terms or provide easy cancellation

penalties.description: ARL violation is also a UCL violation (Bus. & Prof. Code §17200), enabling private right of action for restitution and injunctive relief.

escalation_venues.name: California Attorney General — Consumer Complaint
escalation_venues.description: File a consumer complaint about auto-renewal violations.

escalation_venues.name: California Department of Consumer Affairs
escalation_venues.description: File a complaint with CA DCA.

notes: California ARL is one of the strongest state auto-renewal laws. The 'unconditional gift' provision (§17603) is powerful — if the business didn't comply, the consumer doesn't owe anything. The 2021 amendments (AB 390 / SB 313) significantly strengthened the law by requiring online cancellation for online signups and notification before free-trial-to-paid conversion. UCL private right of action enables individual lawsuits.
